title: AI-Assisted Prediction of Rainwater and Humidity-Induced Degradation in Sustainable Green Batteries: Materials, Mechanisms and Predictive Modeling
content: The transition toward sustainable energy storage requires battery technologies that combine electrochemical performance with reduced environmental impact, resource availability, safety and recyclability. However, environmental exposure, particularly humidity, moisture and rainwater, can adversely affect battery materials and accelerate degradation. Water can participate in electrolyte decomposition, alter electrode/electrolyte interfaces, promote corrosion and modify the structural and electrochemical stability of active materials. Recent studies have demonstrated that humidity can accelerate capacity loss and impedance growth in lithium-ion batteries, while controlled moisture exposure can produce measurable changes in irreversible capacity and internal resistance. This paper proposes an artificial-intelligence-assisted framework for predicting rainwater- and humidity-induced degradation in sustainable green batteries. The framework integrates environmental variables—including relative humidity, temperature, rainfall intensity, exposure duration, dew point and water chemistry—with electrochemical and material descriptors such as capacity retention, internal resistance, impedance, voltage characteristics, mass change and structural parameters. Machine-learning algorithms including random forest, support-vector regression, gradient boosting, artificial neural networks, long short-term memory networks and physics-informed models can be employed to establish relationships between environmental stress and battery degradation. The proposed framework can generate predictions of state of health (SOH), capacity fade, impedance growth and remaining useful life (RUL). Explainable artificial intelligence can further identify the environmental and material factors most strongly associated with degradation. The approach provides a pathway toward climate-resilient battery design, predictive maintenance and environmentally sustainable energy-storage systems.
